added_models.model: Rhesus IV self-administration, rat zolpidem drug discrimination and rat withdrawal (abuse liability battery)

safety.confidence_note: First-use year is a proxy from Merck study report numbers (TT089xxx); the CSS review with the study results is not in the bundle.
safety.note: Merck tested suvorexant for reinforcement in self-administering rhesus, zolpidem-like cueing in rats and withdrawal after 30 days' dosing.
safety.quote: Abuse liability of MK-4305 administered intravenously: Assessment of the relative reinforcing efficacy in Rhesus monkeys maintained to self-administer methohexital.
safety.judgement: Standard nonclinical abuse-liability package, a separate system from the sleep EEG and cataplexy models in the draft.

safety.magnitude_basis: Drug Liking VAS peak vs placebo: animals showed no reinforcement; humans liked suvorexant as much as zolpidem
safety.population: Healthy recreational polydrug users (human abuse potential trial P025)
safety.confidence_note: The review states the sponsor's 'lack of nonclinical evidence of abuse potential' beside Trial P025. The 2019 lemborexant review repeats the pattern ('Nonclinical findings were less suggestive of abuse liability'), and daridorexant's 2022 HAP study matched zolpidem; both are scheduled C-IV.
safety.note: Animals showed no reinforcement or dependence, yet recreational users liked suvorexant as much as zolpidem; it was scheduled C-IV.
safety.short: Animals no abuse; humans liked it
safety.quote: suvorexant in all tested doses (40 mg, 80 mg, and 150 mg) showed greater abuse potential than placebo in recreational polydrug users.
safety.judgement: Model silent on a harm the species battery is built to show (reinforcement); the human abuse potential trial found liking like zolpidem, so contra. The human side is healthy recreational users, the regulator's standard population for this harm.

added_models.model: Mouse emotion-induced (chocolate) cataplexy, wild-type vs preproorexin knockout (lemborexant)

safety.population: C57BL/6J wild-type and preproorexin knockout mice
safety.confidence_note: First-use year is a proxy from the Eisai study number W-20140712; the study is public only in the 2019 FDA review.
safety.note: Lemborexant 10 and 30 mg/kg with chocolate raised cataplexy time in wild-type mice, not in orexin knockouts.
safety.quote: Co-administration of lemborexant (10 and 30 mg/kg) with chocolate statistically significantly increased the time spent in cataplexy in WT mice.
safety.judgement: Different species and trigger from the draft's suvorexant dog food-enrichment model, so a parallel track.

safety.magnitude_basis: Cataplexy-like events: present in mice; rare, unadjudicated leg weakness in patients (2.7-3.0% vs 1.5% placebo on cataplexy-related terms)
safety.population: Adults with insomnia disorder (lemborexant Phase 3 pool)
safety.confidence_note: The reviewer judged cataplexy-related term incidence 'similar in all groups'; one LEM10 case resembled cataplexy but the adjudication committee did not agree. The label nonetheless warns of mild cataplexy-like symptoms.
safety.note: The label warns that mild cataplexy-like leg weakness can occur on lemborexant, as the mouse model showed; no adjudicated cataplexy.
safety.quote: Symptoms similar to mild cataplexy can occur with DAYVIGO. Such symptoms can include periods of leg weakness lasting from seconds to a few minutes
safety.judgement: Paired: the review and label hold the mouse study and the patient events in separate sections. Predicted harm appeared only weakly and unadjudicated, so same with partial, not contra.

added_models.model: PBPK-PD model of brain OX2 receptor occupancy (daridorexant, 65% occupancy threshold)

dose.confidence_note: Abstract read (PMID 28663311). First-use year is a proxy: the model chose ACT-541468 and its dose before the first-in-human trial.
dose.note: Human PK built from in-vitro data predicted OX2 occupancy over the night and an active daridorexant dose of 25 mg.
dose.quote: An active ACT-541468 dose of 25 mg was estimated on the basis of OX2 receptor occupancy thresholds of about 65% derived from clinical data for two other orexin antagonists, almorexant and suvorexant.
dose.judgement: Occupancy threshold calibrated on sibling drugs' clinical data, but the daridorexant dose was predicted before its own trials, so prospective. Treiber also reports the SAD in healthy subjects 'largely confirmed' the PK predictions; that does not test whether the dose was enough.

dose.magnitude_basis: Predicted active dose 25 mg; 25 mg met both PSG primaries in study 1, 50 mg larger, 10 mg failed
dose.confidence_note: Abstracts read (PMID 35065036; Phase 2 PMID 31953863 found a dose-response from 5 to 50 mg, results posted 2020-04-02). In Phase 3 study 2, 25 mg reduced WASO only.
dose.note: Daridorexant 25 mg, the model's predicted active dose, cut WASO and LPS in Phase 3; approved doses are 25 and 50 mg.
dose.quote: WASO and LPS were significantly reduced among participants in the daridorexant 25 mg group compared with the placebo group at month 1
dose.judgement: Paired, not stated. 25 mg reached and worked, 10 mg did not, 50 mg did more: the predicted active dose sat at the low effective end, within 2x.

considered_not_added: Daridorexant PBPK model for CYP3A drug interactions (FDA 2022 review): verified on clinical DDI data and used for labelling, a PK interaction model fitted after the human data, not a prediction for any of the four questions.
Human transient-insomnia / phase-advance challenge models: no member drug found tested in one (PubMed, 2 hits, neither a challenge model).
Mouse comorbid depression-insomnia model (lemborexant, Neuropharmacology 2026): no patient comparison.
Rodent respiratory / sleep-apnea models: no model-to-patient comparison found at abstract level; patient OSA/COPD safety studies exist but name no model prediction.

On-the-road driving and next-day residual-effect tests in healthy elderly (suvorexant 2016): a human measurement, not a model whose prediction was compared with patients; next-day impairment is a rule question raised by the checker.

Preproorexin knockout / orexin-neuron-deficient mice as a target-specificity control (lemborexant): shows on-target action, compared with no patient result beyond the chocolate-cataplexy track added here.
Human PET OX2 occupancy for members: none found; the daridorexant 65% threshold came from almorexant and suvorexant clinical data (folded into the PBPK-PD track).
Vornorexant, fazamorexant, filorexant: no member-specific model differing from the draft's rat/dog EEG found at abstract level.
